items.title: Sumit Sarkar’s unfinished argument with history
items.summary: Sometime in 2000, I lost my copy of Sumit Sarkar’s Modern India in the Hindu College hostel at Delhi University. It was unfortunate. I remember looking for another copy in the library but without any success. I was somehow in a hurry to finish reading it, so I bought a new copy. It was a brown-covered Macmillan copy of the classic. I wasn’t a student of history at the university; his work was there in the interdisciplinary readings. I finished reading the book soon. It has been a matter of wonder for me that Sarkar’s book, which otherwise was a dense and academic study, had engrossed me. The reason wasn’t far to seek. You had to just look at the rest of the bookshelf of readings for the same course. Even if some place the book within a broad Marxist corpus on modern Indian history, Sarkar’s work was remarkable in finding its way out of that dogmatic frame. In doing so, he found a subaltern footing in retelling “history from below”, opening up the narrow economistic gaze of Marxism to social and cultural registers, and noting even the ordinariness of agents shaping modern Indian history. items.title: Plea in Supreme Court seeks criminal action against social media platforms failing to report child porn
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday sought the Central government’s response to a plea seeking implementation of the top court's directions on the mandatory reporting of Child Sexual Exploitation and Abuse Material (CSEAM) by social media intermediaries. [ Just Rights for Children Alliance & Anr. v. S. Harish & Ors] The plea also said there should be criminal action against intermediaries that fail to report CSEAM. A Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and Vinod Chandran issued notice to the government on the plea. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Vinod Chandran The plea was filed by Just Rights for Children Alliance (JRCA) seeking implementation of the Supreme Court’s September 2024 judgment , which held that social media intermediaries are mandatorily required to report offences relating to CSEAM to the concerned police authorities under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO Act) and the rules framed under it. The Court had also held that an intermediary cannot claim protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000 unless it exercises due diligence and complies with its obligations under the POCSO Act and Rules.
